## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), also cited as *Guttilavimāna*, is a canonical verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [von Hinüber 1996; SuttaCentral]. In this text, multiple celestial beings discuss the meritorious actions they performed during their past human lives that led to their rebirth in happy celestial realms [SuttaCentral]. As recorded in the commentary to the *Guttilajātaka* (Ja 243), the Bodhisatta visits the celestial realm and questions thirty-seven goddesses (*devadhītā*) who appear in the *Guttilavimānavatthu*, each explaining in verse the specific karmic deeds—such as offering almsfood or water, maintaining virtue, and serving without anger—that caused their rebirth as companions to the king of gods [Fausböll 1879; SuttaCentral].
Cross-textual connections link this narrative directly with the *Guttilajātaka* (Ja 243) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records 1,851 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 64 texts; extensive textual material is shared with the commentary on the work (*Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*) and with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (notably segments §2.4–10.4 matching §1639–1652 of the second volume), as well as the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, formulaic verses and descriptions are shared with multiple other Vimānavatthu narratives, such as the *Caturitthivimānavatthu* (Vv 45), *Lakhumāvimānavatthu* (Vv 19), *Suniddāvimānavatthu* (Vv 26), *Niddāvimānavatthu* (Vv 25), and *Kañjikadāyikāvimānavatthu* (Vv 43) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages with Sanskrit texts including the *Ratnamālāvadāna* and *Tathāgatabimbakārāpaṇasūtra*, alongside Tibetan canonical texts such as the *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* (D4144) and *Kāraṇaprajñapti* (D4087) [DharmaNexus].
